name: Logistic Regression
tagline: The bedrock of linear classification: mapping linear combinations to probabilities.
introduction: Despite its name, Logistic Regression is a classification algorithm. It extends linear regression by passing a linear combination of input features through the non-linear sigmoid (logistic) activation function. This constrains predictions strictly between 0 and 1, allowing them to be interpreted as the probability of belonging to the positive class.
why_used: Provides well-calibrated probabilistic outputs rather than just discrete class labels.
Highly interpretable: model coefficients directly represent the change in log-odds per unit change in each feature.
Computationally lightweight and extraordinarily fast to train and evaluate.
Serves as the universal gold-standard baseline for binary and multiclass classification tasks.
how_it_works:
1. Compute a linear score z = w_1*x_1 + w_2*x_2 + ... + w_n*x_n + b.
2. Pass z into the sigmoid function: sigma(z) = 1 / (1 + e^(-z)).
3. This maps any real-valued number into a probability between 0 and 1.
4. Predict class 1 if sigma(z) >= 0.5 (or any user-defined threshold), otherwise predict class 0.
5. Optimize weights using gradient-based solvers to minimize Binary Cross-Entropy (Log Loss).
mathematical_intuition: Linear regression fits a straight line, which can predict values less than 0 or greater than 1—invalid for probabilities. The sigmoid function provides an 'S-shaped' curve that maps (-infinity, +infinity) smoothly to (0, 1). The log-odds (logit) of probability p is a linear function of features: ln(p / (1 - p)) = w^T * x + b.

important_formulas.name: Sigmoid (Logistic) Function
important_formulas.description: Squashes any continuous linear score z into a probability range [0, 1].

important_formulas.name: Log-Odds (Logit)
important_formulas.formula: \ln\left(\frac{p}{1 - p}\right) = w_0 + w_1 x_1 + ... + w_n x_n
important_formulas.description: The logarithm of the odds of the event occurring is a linear combination of input features.

important_formulas.name: Binary Cross-Entropy Loss (Log Loss)
important_formulas.description: Convex loss function penalizing confident wrong predictions heavily.

step_by_step_example.scenario: Predicting loan default probability based on credit score (x1) and debt-to-income ratio (x2).
step_by_step_example.decision: At 0.5 threshold: 0.4013 < 0.5, so the model predicts 'No Default' (Class 0).

advantages: High interpretability: feature weights explain directional importance and odds ratio multipliers.
Outputs calibrated probabilities, essential for risk scoring and threshold tuning.
Very fast training and minimal memory footprint; ideal for real-time systems.
Less prone to overfitting in low dimensions, especially when L1 or L2 regularization is applied.
disadvantages: Assumes a linear relationship between input features and the log-odds of the target.
Cannot capture non-linear relationships or complex feature interactions without manual feature engineering.
Requires feature scaling (e.g. StandardScaler) for reliable gradient convergence and fair L1/L2 regularization.
Sensitive to severe multicollinearity between features.
when_to_use: When model explainability and compliance are legally or operationally required (e.g. credit underwriting).
When class probabilities are needed to set risk-sensitive decision thresholds.
As the primary linear baseline before trying complex non-linear models.
when_to_avoid: When complex non-linear boundaries are known to exist and cannot be linearized.
When many correlated categorical features have high cardinality without sufficient training samples.

comparison_with_related.difference: Linear Regression predicts continuous numbers (-inf to +inf); Logistic Regression predicts bounded probabilities (0 to 1) via the sigmoid transform.
Logistic Regression creates a single smooth linear hyperplane; Decision Trees create orthogonal stepwise partitions.

practical_example: Spam email filtering: predicting whether an email is spam (1) or ham (0) based on word frequencies and sender reputation.
